To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the sustainability of electronic health information system investments is likely to be affected by the following: 1) the ability of the health information system to be used by the intended users; 2) the ability of health information system users to maintain and upgrade the system as needed; 3) the ability of stakeholders to integrate the health information system with other activities within and outside the health system; and 4) the ability of all stakeholders to work together in the long term.

the sustainability of EHIS depends on a combination of factors including: 1) the system is designed to meet the needs of the country and is integrated with the rest of the health system; 2) there is a clear plan for the transition to the system; 3) there are adequate resources and a plan to maintain the system; and 4) the system is well supported by stakeholders.

the sustainability of EHIS is threatened by technical resource constraints affecting usage, maintenance, repairs, and upgrades, and by a lack of stakeholder engagement, integration with other activities and a clearly defined goal around which stakeholders can mobilize.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the sustainability of EHIS, which is defined as the ability of the health systems to maintain and enhance EHIS in the future.
the sustainability of EHIS in three countries, but the lessons are likely to be relevant to other countries and other types of health information systems.
the sustainability of EHIS in Malawi, Zimbabwe and Zambia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
EHIS are not likely to be sustainable in their current forms, but that with careful planning they can be made more sustainable.

the sustainability of EHIS is likely to be enhanced by: (i) a clearly articulated vision of how the system is to be used, (ii) the development of a strong and coordinated stakeholder network, and (iii) the building of organizational and technical capacity to manage the system.
the systems studied are not currently sustainable, but with attention to the issues highlighted in this paper, the sustainability of the EHIS in these three countries could be improved.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
sustainability of EHIS requires a focus on both the system and the environment.
there are no quick fixes for sustainability.
a sustainable health information system should be seen as a long term investment that is built on a solid foundation of technical design, stakeholders' commitment and organizational capacity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the sustainability of EHIS should be considered from the beginning and not as an afterthought.
sustainability of EHIS is not a binary outcome, but a continuum.
there are a number of factors that may influence EHIS sustainability, which should be considered when designing, implementing, and evaluating such systems in the future.
